**Visual observations:**
- Very early seedling stage, just emerging from soil
- Cotyledons/seed visible at soil level — the seed/cotyledon appears green/intact but the seedling is barely emerged
- To the right, a second seedling appears collapsed/dead — brown, shriveled, rotted cotyledons lying in the soil
- The failed seedling shows water-soaked, collapsed, rotted tissue at the soil line
- Wet soil conditions visible (muddy, moist environment)
- This is clearly a damping-off situation — one seedling is struggling to emerge while another has already collapsed and rotted

**Reasoning:**
- The scene shows pre/post-emergence damping off in wet soil conditions
- The collapsed seedling to the right shows brown, soft, rotted tissue — consistent with water-soaked lesions becoming brown soft rot
- Wet, muddy soil is the classic environment for Pythium
- Rhizoctonia would show reddish-brown, firm, dry cankers — not the soft, water-soaked collapse visible here
- Phytophthora causes similar damping off but typically shows a chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending upward; this appears to be at or below the soil line with soft collapse
- Pythium damping-off matches perfectly: rotted seeds/seedlings in wet soil, water-soaked lesions turning to brown soft rot, pre/postemergence collapse
